learning_expectations.question_text: What are you hoping to learn or take away from this specific workshop?  What questions or topics do you hope this workshop will cover?.

responses:
I am hoping to get a good understanding of the next topics in the Computer Science Principles course.  So far, we have done mostly unplugged lessons at this point in the school year.  I have noticed that a few of my students have access to the teacher version of the course and I want to know how to remove that before we start doing plugged activities in class.  The teacher who teaches the other section has one student who cannot seem to access her section, and if I cannot figure that out tomorrow, I may need help with that.

The lessons are designed for 45 minutes, in theory, but sometimes I have a little time left over and other times we have to finish something up the next time we meet, so clearly, I could use some help with pacing, too.

I would like to learn how to keep the class engaged especially when different people finish early,  having something for them to continue working on instead of wasting time. I think some of the lessons with choices, having them go back to them to do some things they did not and refresh their memory on the topics covered already.
I look forward to learning how to implement all the Code.org lessons for my classes.
Guidance on how execute this course with a way of understanding it myself.
I to properly teach Coding in the high school settings.

other_feedback_FR.question_text: Is there anything else you’d like to tell us about your experience at this workshop?

responses: This has been WONDERFUL. I prepped the BETA version of this course all spring and am SO HAPPY to have this workshop on the new course and see how different it is from APCSP (the other CS class I teach) - I will sign up for one of these every summer!!!!

Wish that code.org gave us full blown examples on how lesson being taught. Especially in the coding part. SO we can show the kids the an example on what is being taught with the code being taught. There no real example. even the teacher example is incomplete.
This is great!  Keep it up.  I look forward to next year!

I alway enjoy meeting up with old friends and making new friends. 
Learning what others are doing in their classroom, especially the classroom projects. 
I enjoyed the evening options to learn more about different vendors.
This was a very helpful experience, and I feel much better about the upcoming semester now than I did coming in.
Some of the bugs of Code.org looked obvious and untouched.

I felt more prepared teaching CSD (the session I did last year) versus this class.  It felt like we saw more lessons in action.  This year I felt like we were looking at the course more on our own.  Maybe because it is new?
I don't love the TLOs but I see their role in the process.
